title: This Spider Mother Melts Her Own Insides, Then Her Babies Eat Her

scenes.text: This spider mother is cooking herself for dinner.
scenes.keywords: velvet spider on web close up

scenes.text: Stegodyphus lineatus lays a single clutch in her life, in the deserts of Israel and the Middle East.
As soon as the eggs are laid, her gut begins to break down. Her stored fat turns to liquid inside her abdomen.
When the spiderlings hatch, she feeds them that liquid, mouth to mouth, for about two weeks.
By then most of her abdomen is soup. The young climb onto her and drink her completely, leaving an empty shell.
She never tries to escape. In a related species, even childless aunts liquefy themselves for their sisters' babies. Dinner is served.

description:
Female velvet spiders of the genus Stegodyphus practice matriphagy: after laying her only clutch, the mother's digestive tissue degenerates and her abdomen liquefies; she regurgitates the liquid to her spiderlings for about two weeks, and then they consume her entirely, leaving an empty exoskeleton.
In the social species Stegodyphus dumicola, unmated females also feed and are eaten by their relatives' young (Salomon et al., Journal of Arachnology, 2015; Junghanns et al., Animal Behaviour, 2017).
What is the most extreme parenting you know of in nature?
subject: velvet spider
first_comment: Her ovaries and heart are the last organs to dissolve, so if the babies are taken away she can still lay a second clutch. Which animal parent sacrifices the most?
